text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1  API reachability degraded  elevated 5xx & TLS handshake failures observed across multiple Cloudflare POPs for api.redwood.ai. Pager window triggered.

olga: spotting customer errors and Slack escalations. Our mobile clients show failures to establish TLS, some users get 502/524. Repro with curl: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (104.21.20.33) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 handshake, Client hello
* TLS 1.3 handshake, Server hello
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, certificate unknown
* SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
* Closing connection 0
```
(also seeing `tls: handshake failure` in internal ELBs)

oncall-ryan: I'm oncall. Initial triage: origin logs (NLB + gateway) look healthy, backend requests returning 200. Failures terminate at CF edge. Cloudflare status shows partial TLS issues.

cf-status-bot: Cloudflare incident 7890: "Customers experiencing TLS handshake failures in select POPs. Engineers investigating." https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/7890

kevin-support: Support queue filling up fast. I'll post a brief customer-facing note and prepped troubleshooting steps for accounts team.

sre-manager: mitigation options: 
- Rapid: Create a direct-origin DNS alias (api-origin.redwood.ai) for critical customers to bypass Cloudflare proxy and terminate TLS at our gateway.
- Short-term: Adjust Cloudflare SSL/TLS setting to 'Full (strict) -> Full' to reduce strict-chain checks (but this may not help if edge is failing).
- Longer: Work with CF to roll back recent edge config if they identify a bad deploy.
We should prefer targeted direct-origin fallback to avoid broad DNS churn.

oncall-ryan: I'll provision api-origin with a low-ttl CNAME and map on gateway; bind the existing wildcard cert issued by our ACME CA. I'll only advertise this to select customers (top 5 by error volume) to limit blast radius.

okta-alerts: Okta reports elevated token exchange latency in US-east; some downstream 401s observed but likely secondary to TLS issues.

olga: Noted. Datadog shows metric gaps in traces ingestion — we may have blind spots while CF is degraded.

datadog-bot: Warning: traces ingestion delay 12m. Dashboard snapshots attached.

kevin-support: Drafting customer message: 
"We're investigating intermittent TLS handshake failures impacting API calls in some regions. We're routing critical customers to a direct origin path temporarily; no data loss is expected. We'll update here and on status.redwood.ai."

oncall-ryan: Action plan executed: 
1) Created api-origin.redwood.ai (CNAME -> origin-nlb.redwood.net) with TTL=60.
2) Updated gateway vhost to accept Host header api-origin.redwood.ai and attached cert wildcard.redwood.ai.
3) Re-routed traffic for 5 customers via DNS change on their side (we sent instructions) and via header rewrite for proxy partners.
4) Opened Cloudflare support ticket CF-7890, requested edge engineer escalation; provided PCAPs, example client IPs, and reproducible curl output.
Ticket: https://support.cloudflare.com/cases/CF-7890

olga: Early numbers: those routed to origin show TLS success and 200s. Overall error rate dropped from ~18% -> ~6% in the next 10m for routed customers. Non-routed customers still affected.

sre-manager: Keep retry/backoff settings for public API a bit more aggressive: add 3 retries with exponential backoff and randomized jitter for 502/524 and TLS handshake failures. Ensure idempotency guards for unsafe endpoints.

kevin-support: Sent instructions and fallback DNS entry to account teams and affected customers. Template includes steps to switch to api-origin and expected certificate CN.

oncall-ryan: Observability notes: Datadog logs delayed; use gateway access logs and origin LB metrics for live monitoring. I'm streaming logs to a separate ephemeral index to avoid CF ingestion dependency.

cf-status-bot: Cloudflare update: "Deploying mitigation to affected POPs, monitoring improvements."

olga: After CF mitigation note, overall errors decreased but we still see regional flaps. Okta latency also seems to normalize, so 401 rate decreasing.

sre-manager: Prepare rollback plan: 
- Once CF marks incident resolved and we see stable <=1% TLS failures for 30m, revert customers back to api.redwood.ai gradually by restoring original CNAME and dropping api-origin entries.
- Verify cert chain & OCSP stapling post-switch.
- Run smoke tests from EU and US-east clients.

kevin-support: Posted incident blurb on status.redwood.ai and emailed high-touch customers.

oncall-ryan: Handoff: I'm handing active incident to olga at 1820460200. All temporary routing changes documented in the runbook: /runbooks/incidents/cf-tls-fallback (internal). Keep CF ticket updated; request full post-incident timeline from them.

olga: Taking over. I'll monitor TLS failure ratio, Cloudflare updates, and support queue. Will coordinate rollback once CF confirms fix and our metrics are green for 30m.

sre-manager: Thanks team  good quick mitigation. We'll run a postmortem next week; include decision timeline, why direct-origin chosen, and any improvements to automations for future third-party edge failures.

oncall-ryan: Leaving notes: saved pcap + curl output + affected IP list in incident artifact S3 (s3://redwood-incidents/1820456789/).

kevin-support: Final customer impact summary for comms: 
- Incident start: 1820456789
- Mitigation: direct-origin fallback for 5 high-QPS customers; retries/backoff enabled; CF escalated
- Scope: peak ~18% error rate across EU & US-east; reduced to ~5% for routed customers, overall 7% after mitigations
- Services impacted: API reachability, increased 502/524, TLS handshake failures; transient auth 401s due to Okta latency
- Current status: partial mitigation in place; Cloudflare implementing fixes; monitoring handover to olga.

olga: Acknowledged. I'll keep this thread updated and will post when we start rollback. :thumbsup:
__note: Single Slack thread string, messages prefixed by sender names per agents.md. No title field included.
